title: Pollo Asado Chicken Thigh Bowl
summary: Citrus-achiote thighs seared hard for char, over brown rice with black beans, mango habanero salsa, cotija, and blended cottage cheese. Three builds: skinless, skin-on, and Costco precooked.

builds.label: Costco precooked
builds.note: Costco's precooked pollo asado in place of the thighs and marinade.

ingredients.raw: 1.5 lb precooked Costco pollo asado (3/4 of a 2 lb bag)
1 tbsp achiote paste (or 1 tbsp sweet paprika + 1/4 tsp turmeric)
1 tbsp adobo sauce from a can of chipotles (optional, adds smoky heat)
1 cup dry brown rice (~3 cups cooked, 3/4 cup per bowl), tossed with lime zest and chopped cilantro
1 can (15oz) black beans, drained, plus cumin and garlic powder
4 oz cotija, crumbled (1 oz, about 1/4 cup, per bowl)
3/4 cup 2% cottage cheese, blended smooth (3 tbsp per bowl). Add 1 tbsp milk only if the blender won't catch

steps.body: Whisk the marinade and coat the thighs. Refrigerate 2 to 4 hr, never past 6. The citrus turns the texture mushy.
Make the mango habanero salsa so it has at least 15 min to sit.
Blend the cottage cheese until silky. Refrigerate.
Crumble the cotija fine so it spreads across the whole bowl.
Pull the thighs from the marinade and let the excess drip off. Sear in a ripping hot cast iron pan, 5 to 6 min per side, in batches, until charred and 175°F. Rest 5 min, then chop.

Pat the skin completely dry after marinating. Place skin-side down in a cold-to-medium dry pan and render 6 to 8 min until deep golden. Pour off all but about 1 tsp of fat, flip, and cook 6 to 8 min more until 175°F, or finish in a 400°F oven. Rest 5 min, then slice and plate skin-side up.
Sear the precooked chicken in a very hot dry cast iron pan, 2 to 3 min per side, until the edges char. Finish with a squeeze of lime, then chop.
Warm the black beans with the cumin and garlic powder.
Build each bowl: 3/4 cup rice, a quarter of the beans, 6 oz chicken, 1/2 cup salsa, 1 oz cotija, and 3 tbsp blended cottage cheese.

notes.body: Every build uses 6 oz of chicken and 1 oz of cotija per bowl. Homemade is 6 oz raw, and Costco is 6 oz as packaged. The traditional row assumes skin-on thighs, white rice, an oil-heavy marinade, sour cream, and the same cotija.

Skinless lands at 27% fat, inside the 25 to 30% target. Dropping the cotija to 3/4 oz brings it to about 25% (645 cal, 18g fat, 55g protein). Skin-on runs about 33% fat, above the target, so it's the build for days when your fat is running low. Sodium is roughly 1,100mg per bowl, mostly from the cotija, beans, and chicken seasoning.
**Get the pan ripping hot.** Char is what makes it asado, and a crowded pan steams the thighs instead
**Marinate 2 to 4 hours, not overnight.** Past 6 hr the acid breaks the meat down
**Let the excess marinade drip off before searing.** Wet chicken steams and won't char
**Skin-on: dry the skin, render it first, pour off the fat.** The skin-on numbers assume you do. Leave it all in and add about 3g fat per bowl
**Cotija goes on cold, last, and crumbled fine.** It doesn't melt, so fine crumbles spread the salt and cut the habanero heat
**Blend the cottage cheese fully.** Any grain shows when it's served cold
**Hold the salt until the end.** Cotija, beans, and the chicken seasoning already carry plenty
**No char:** the pan wasn't hot enough or the chicken was wet. Heat longer and pat off more marinade
**Too salty:** squeeze more lime and add extra salsa. Next time drop the cotija to 3/4 oz or use rinsed beans, which saves about 100mg
**Chicken mushy:** it marinated too long. Stay inside 2 to 4 hr
**Flat flavor:** the marinade is lighter on acid, so finish with a squeeze of lime from the wedges
**Salsa too hot:** add more mango and lime, and spoon extra cottage cheese over the bowl
**Chicken dry:** pull at 175°F and rest before cutting
